intro: To add SmartArt in PowerPoint on Mac, open the Insert tab, select SmartArt, point at a type in the menu that appears, and choose a layout. Then type your text in the Text pane or directly in the shapes.
tldr: Open the Insert tab, select SmartArt, point at a type in the menu, then pick a layout.
Type in the Text pane. If it is hidden, select the arrow on the graphic's left side.
Add shapes with the arrow next to Add Shape on the SmartArt Design tab.
Change colors and styles on the same tab, using Change Colors and More.
Some Mac users reported an oversized text pane after the 16.98 update, so test before a big deck.

blocks.text: SmartArt turns a list of ideas into a diagram. You type the points, and PowerPoint arranges them into a process, a cycle, a hierarchy or a list. You can swap the layout later without rebuilding the graphic. That is the main reason to use it over drawing boxes and arrows by hand.
Check your version before you start

Microsoft's SmartArt article covers PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 for Mac, PowerPoint 2024 and PowerPoint 2021. Older versions may have different menus. Open PowerPoint, then choose PowerPoint > About PowerPoint to see your build. The article gives no Mac build number.

The latest Mac build in Microsoft's release notes is 16.114.3, dated 27 October 2026. Those notes describe it as quality and performance improvements. They do not mention SmartArt or the Insert tab. A newer build is not a guaranteed fix for any SmartArt issue.

items: Microsoft 365 for Mac, or PowerPoint 2024 or 2021, as listed in Microsoft's SmartArt article.
macOS 12 Monterey or later to install Office 16.78 or newer.
macOS 14 Sonoma or later to keep receiving updates for Microsoft 365 and Office apps.
Your macOS version is under Apple menu > About This Mac.

blocks.text: Office still runs on older macOS versions. It stops getting updates, including security updates. Treat that as the real risk. A diagram is easy to redo. Missing security updates are much harder to live with.
Choose a layout that fits your content

Layouts work best when your text already has a shape. A process has steps in order. A hierarchy has a top level and branches. A cycle repeats. If you only have a few loose facts, a plain bulleted list may do the job faster.

Pick a layout, then test it with your real text. Long labels crowd small layouts quickly. Switch layouts before you resize shapes by hand. Hand resizing fights the layout, and the graphic gets messy when you add the next item.
Edit text in the Text pane and shapes
The Text pane is the fastest way to edit. Each line in the pane is one shape. Add a line, and you add a shape. Keep the pane open while you restructure, so you can see the whole structure at once.
To add a shape next to a specific box, select the nearest shape first. Then open the SmartArt Design tab and select the arrow next to Add Shape. Pick the placement you need from the menu that opens.

Say you want a diagram of a project plan with a few stages. Start with a process layout, since the stages happen in order. Type each stage name in the Text pane. Then add a sub-task under the stage that needs one, using the Add Shape arrow. Change colors last, once the content is set.
If you paste text from another app, its formatting can come with it. Use Paste Special with ⌘⌃V and choose plain text. Plain text keeps the diagram's look consistent with the rest of the graphic.
Add a title and a text box

Microsoft's article uses a text box for a title near the graphic. Insert the text box above or beside the graphic. Control-click the text box, then choose Format Shape, or Format, depending on your version. Match the font and size to the rest of the slide.
Set colors and styles without breaking the slide

With the graphic selected, open the SmartArt Design tab. Change Colors applies a color set across the shapes. The More button in the styles group shows the full gallery. Pick one, then check that text stays readable on the new fill.

A bright color set can clash with your deck's theme. If your brand uses specific colors, compare them with the slide master first. For that, see [how to edit the slide master in PowerPoint](/how-to/edit-the-slide-master-in-powerpoint).
Keyboard shortcuts for SmartArt on Mac

Microsoft's PowerPoint for Mac shortcut list has no SmartArt entry. Its Office for Mac list has no shortcut for the Insert tab either. You will use the menu path for the insert step. These shortcuts still help while you build the graphic.

items: ⌘⌥R expands or minimizes the ribbon, so the SmartArt Design tab stays on screen.
⌘⇧1 formats the selected object, according to Microsoft's PowerPoint list.
⌘⇧C and ⌘⇧V copy and paste formatting, useful when one shape needs the same look as another.

blocks.text: The Mac text pane bug and what to try

In July 2025, people in a Microsoft Q&A thread reported an oversized SmartArt text pane on PowerPoint for Mac. They also reported misaligned cursor clicks and scrolling trouble. A Microsoft moderator linked the problems to the update to version 16.98 from June 2025.

The thread lists a few workarounds. Connect an external display. Edit through View > Outline View. Or change the display resolution to 1920 x 1200 with PowerPoint closed. Results were mixed, so treat each one as a test, not a fix.

One user said Outline View showed no SmartArt text. The resolution change did not help that person, and the problem stayed after an update. I found no official fix. The threads date from July 2025, so the current status is unconfirmed. Test on a spare slide before you build a large diagram.
SmartArt in PowerPoint for the web

The web app has SmartArt too. Open the Insert tab, select SmartArt, and choose a layout from the dropdown. A text editor opens on the left, and you type there. The SmartArt tab holds colors, styles, Right to Left, and Promote and Demote.

Microsoft's web-feature page lists inserting a graphic, switching the layout or color scheme, applying styles, and editing text. It does not list the desktop-only limits. So the web app is not a full stand-in for the Mac app. Test the file in both if others will open it on the web.
Mistakes people make with SmartArt

items: Drawing boxes and arrows by hand. Rebuilding that later often takes longer than the graphic would have.
Packing long sentences into each shape. Keep labels short, or the layout will crowd.
Forgetting the Text pane is hidden, then searching the slide for the text.
Resizing shapes by hand instead of switching the layout.
Assuming the Windows menu path works. On Mac, start at Insert > SmartArt.
Skipping the version check before a client deck goes out.

blocks.text: What to do next
Build one test graphic with your real text. Then open the slide show and check that every label fits. Read each label once more before you present.
Keep Office current, and save a copy before you change a layout on a finished diagram. If the text pane misbehaves, duplicate the slide and test the fix there first.
When the deck is ready to present, [how to use Presenter View in PowerPoint on Mac](/how-to/use-presenter-view-in-powerpoint) covers the speaker's side of the screen.

faq.question: Where is SmartArt on a Mac?
faq.answer: Open the Insert tab and select SmartArt. Microsoft's Mac steps say this. The Windows steps use Insert > Illustrations > SmartArt, but the Mac article does not mention an Illustrations group, so check your ribbon if it looks different.

faq.question: Which PowerPoint versions include SmartArt?
faq.answer: Microsoft's SmartArt article lists PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 for Mac, PowerPoint 2024 and PowerPoint 2021. It gives no Mac build number, so check your version under PowerPoint > About PowerPoint.

faq.question: Do I need the newest version of macOS?
faq.answer: You need macOS 12 Monterey or later to install Office 16.78 or newer. You need macOS 14 Sonoma or later to keep receiving updates for Microsoft 365 and Office apps. Older systems keep working but get no updates.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to insert SmartArt?
faq.answer: Not one that Microsoft documents. Its PowerPoint for Mac shortcut list has no SmartArt entry, and its Office for Mac list has no shortcut for the Insert tab. Use the menu path.

faq.question: Can I switch a SmartArt graphic to another layout later?
faq.answer: Microsoft's web-feature page says you can switch layout in PowerPoint for the web. The Mac article I checked does not spell out that step. Look for the layout options on the SmartArt Design tab, and confirm them in your build.

faq.question: Why does my SmartArt text pane look too big on Mac?
faq.answer: A Microsoft Q&A thread from July 2025 reports this after the 16.98 update, released in June 2025. A moderator linked the problems to that update. I found no official fix, so test on a spare slide first.

faq.question: Does SmartArt work in PowerPoint for the web?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the Insert tab, select SmartArt, pick a layout from the dropdown, then type in the text editor on the left. The SmartArt tab holds colors, styles, Right to Left, and Promote and Demote.

steps.name: Open the Insert tab
steps.text: Open your presentation and go to the slide where the graphic belongs. Click the Insert tab in the ribbon at the top of the window. Make sure the ribbon is fully open, since the commands sit in it.
steps.tip: If the ribbon is collapsed, press ⌘⌥R to expand it again.

steps.name: Open the SmartArt menu
steps.text: On the Insert tab, select SmartArt. A menu opens with the SmartArt types you can choose from.
steps.tip: Microsoft's Mac steps describe this menu. The Windows steps use a different group, so check your ribbon.

steps.name: Point at a type
steps.text: Point at a type in the menu. Its layouts appear, so you can see what each one looks like before you commit.

steps.name: Select a layout
steps.text: Select the layout you want. The graphic lands on the slide, ready for your text.

steps.name: Add your text
steps.text: Type in the Text pane. Each line you type becomes a shape. If the pane is hidden, select the arrow on the left side of the graphic to open it.
menuPath: Arrow on the graphic's left side

steps.name: Add or remove shapes
steps.text: Select the shape closest to the spot where you want the new one. On the SmartArt Design tab, select the arrow next to Add Shape. Pick the placement you need from the menu that opens.
steps.tip: To remove a shape, select it and press the Delete key.

steps.name: Change colors and style
steps.text: With the graphic selected, open the SmartArt Design tab. Select Change Colors to pick a color set. Select More in the styles group to open the full style gallery.
steps.tip: Check that text stays readable on the new fill before you move on.

steps.name: Add a title with a text box
steps.text: Add a text box above or beside the graphic for a title. Control-click the text box, then choose Format Shape, or Format, depending on your version.
steps.tip: Microsoft's article suggests a text box for a title near the graphic.

troubleshooting.problem: The text pane is oversized or clicks land in the wrong spot
troubleshooting.fix: Microsoft Q&A users reported this on PowerPoint for Mac from July 2025, after the 16.98 update. Try an external display or View > Outline View. One user said Outline View showed no SmartArt text, so check your result.
Select the arrow on the left side of the graphic. Microsoft's article describes this control. If the arrow is out of view, zoom out and select the graphic first.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot find SmartArt on the Insert tab
troubleshooting.fix: Check your build under PowerPoint > About PowerPoint. Microsoft's SmartArt article gives no Mac build number, but the latest build in the release notes is 16.114.3. Update, then look again.

troubleshooting.problem: Shape text is too big for the shape
troubleshooting.fix: Shorten the labels or choose a layout with more room for text. Resizing shapes by hand usually makes the layout worse.
